title: Exclusive Elves Vanyar Pro 2024 Unbox, Review & In-Depth Analysis… Game Changer or Overhyped?

takeaways.text: The seatpost stopped short on an internal safety ridge; Elves said sizes 47–53 get a 350 mm post and 56–59 a 400 mm post, so his 400 mm post had to be cut. Only a hint of overspray was found on the fork crown race.
The PF386 shell bores measured on the 46 mm target and headset seats 52.1–52.3 mm with snug, play-free bearing fits; the chainstay is marked with a 100 kg maximum rider weight.
Elves rates 30 mm tires; a 32 mm tire on a carbon rim spun but left minimal room under the rear, while a 28 mm GP5000 had comfortable clearance, so he recommends 28 mm.
Early UK sample, size 50: frame 1,000 g against an 870 g unpainted size-47 claim; fork 417 g (430 g claimed), seatpost 236 g (215 g claimed), PF386 bottom bracket 117 g, thru-axles 77 g.
Expected price about £800 (about US$1,018) in August 2023 for the frameset with a five-year warranty card.

disclosure: The creator discloses occasional commissions on equipment links. The description does not establish frame-supply terms for this first look.
summary: First look at the explicitly named Vanyar Pro Disc 2024, published in 2023. It is unboxing context, not a long-term ride test or evidence for older Vanyar frames.
